summary: I checked the draft against all four examinations and the reviews. I also read config.py, app.py and requirements.txt, and the cited lines match the findings. IDs, severities and decisions are stated as the input gives them, and the hygiene section no longer mentions an earlier draft, which answers RV-6-C1. One minor wording problem remains.

challenges.claim: The known_vulnerabilities section says 'The reviewer could not independently query OSV, so advisory details were not independently verified.' That sentence passes review history into client-facing text. The insecure_config section also credits the unauthenticated-endpoints note to 'the reviewer', when it came from the examiner's own limitations.
challenges.rationale: The disposition says not to refer to earlier drafts or review history in client-facing text. The OSV caveat comes from the RV-5 review summary, not from the examination's own limitations, which only say express and gunicorn were not queried and that no lockfile exists. The unauthenticated /orders and charge routes are real in app.py, but the examiner raised that point, so 'the reviewer' is the wrong attribution. Both sentences should be rewritten as plain statements that advisory data was not independently re-verified and that the endpoints lack authentication.
